_comment: Wave 1 -- one dial at a time against a byte-identical opponent (agents/champ/k01.py). _TRACE is the same in every arm, so planting, harvesting, hiring and buying never vary; only market behaviour does. Any deviation from 50% is caused by the dial and nothing else.
_dials_deliberately_not_tested: _RESERVE, _RAMP_START, _RAMP_END and _SHED_PRESSURE are read only inside _plan_sells, which iterates `for item in _RESERVE` -- empty in every agent in this repo. They are provably inert, and _RESERVE is worse than inert: setting it strips the tape's SELL orders and re-plans them from the turn's opening shed, which cannot see goods dropped this turn. Measured seed 777: wool listed 136 -> 63 units, bank $63,550 -> $43,073. See tools/perturb.py.

_notes.C_front_run: _X_SELL_FROM={item: 0} replaces the tape's SELL orders for that product with one oversized SELL in slot 0. The engine resolves market orders index by index across both players, so slot 0 prices before the opponent's matching order. Same goods, same total -- only the slot and the timing within the turn change.
_notes.D_contrast: Identical to C but _X_SLOT=-1, the latest slot. C minus D isolates slot position from everything else the oversized order changes. Without this pair, a C effect could not be attributed to front-running.
_notes.E_bomb: Suppress the product entirely, let it pile up in the shed, then list it all at once. Cost is real and known: the shed holds 100 and end-of-day overflow is discarded, so a four-product hoard starves every other deposit. E.fuse_wool_d20 hoards one product only and is the cheap version of the same idea.
_notes.F_clone_detector: The donor's _front_run fires only when its mirror detector is confident (_CLONE_CONFIDENCE >= 2), which self-play is exactly the case for. Wrap.py's docstring claims it never fires; these arms decide that.
_notes.H_buy_side: BUY_PRODUCT drains inventory and lifts the price. Only WHEAT and FERTILIZER can be bought. Fertilizer has no other sink anywhere in the engine -- no shop and no town-centre line consumes it -- so its inventory falls only when somebody buys. We list ~1,708 units of fertilizer a season and close it near $1; these arms ask whether the party on the other side of that is getting something for nothing.
_notes.wheat_is_the_control_product: C.fr_wheat should do little: WHEAT's price floor is $17 and it takes more than 20,000 units to get there, so it cannot be crashed. If it moves like C.fr_wool, the effect is not about market depth and the whole reading changes.
